newsitem.title: USA: McCormick confirms federal probe, defends contracts.
newsitem.headline: McCormick confirms federal probe, defends contracts.

text.p: McCormick & Co. Inc. Thursday confirmed that the government is probing whether the food and spice maker is engaging in unfair competition by requiring that certain customers make it their sole supplier.
McCormick defended the exclusivity agreements, saying they were used in a small number of cases and were "appropriate and not an unfair method of competition."

"We firmly believe that we have not engaged in any unethical marketing practices," said McCormick President Robert Lawless, adding that reports suggesting the contrary were "absolutely outrageous, unfounded and offensive."
In a statement, McCormick said it had not prevously reported its use of exclusivity clauses "because it is immaterial."

It said the Federal Trade Commission has made no determination that the clauses constitute an unfair practice and that there are no claims for damages, whether punitive or otherwise, against Sparks, Md.-based McCormick.

In a report Thursday, the Wall Street Journal quoted a Prudential Securities analyst, John McMillin, as saying that news of the investigation surfaced in an analysts' conference call earlier this week with Australia's Burns, Philp & Co., which is a McCormick competitor.

McMillin had said, according to the account, that Burns Philp officials stated at the conference call that the FTC had sought information from the Australian company as part of the McCormick investigation.
McCormick's stock fell 37.5 cents to $25.75 on the New York Stock Exchange.
